page.layout: One printed page, one column of running text with marginal notes in the right margin (two short italic notes beside the text at the level of the paragraph starting "Ad hunc ergo modum"). Running head at top centre. Page number at top right. No text below the main column.

main_text.p: IX. Quanquam quomodo fcribendi deftitui ar-gumento pofsis non video, cum in peregrinatione i-fta multa te videre: audire multa: multis multorum interesse colloquiis necesse fit.
X. Interim tamen, vt verum fatear, illa ipfa tua peregrinatio follicitum tui in me defiderium parit.
XI. Amici etiam & cognati tui, quàm te expe-ctent auidè, ex ipforum ad te datis literis cognofces.
XII. Itaq; operam dabis: vt abfoluto ftudiorum curfu totoq; itinere è fententia confecto, primo quaque tempore ad nos redeas.
XIII. Neq; committas, vt idem tibi quod Vlyßi accidat, qui ex longa atq; diuturna peregrinatione domum reuerfus à fuis agnofci amplius non potuit.

Ad hunc ergo modum aperte & directo ab amico petere aliquid poterimus.Quod Oblique & tecte petitionessi vero oblique funt tecteq; petitiones in-ftituedæ: vel quia res ipfa quâ petimus pa-rum honefta, vtilis, facilis effe videtur: vel quia is ad quem fcribimus, non vfq; ad ò nobis fauet: vel nos minus verecundè atq; modefte rogare illud iudicari poffumus, quod ad noftram laudem ac gloriam facit: ad imitandum maximè proponi poterit epift.12.lib.15.2.lib.11.4.lib.15. Et.8.lib.10. ad Atticum in qua Antonius admodum artificiosè Ciceronem rogat; ne cum Pom

page.notes: Marginal note at right reads "Oblique & tecte petitiones" (two lines, the second partly cut). Some words in the top paragraphs are blurred by the scan; "fcribendi" and "interesse" read with some uncertainty. The printed text ends mid-sentence at "cum Pom" (Pompeium). Short-s and italic marking follow the scan; last lines are slightly cramped at the page edge. The printed note "nes." sits beneath "petitiones" and is part of the same margin note.
